name: whisperr
description: Install the Whisperr SDK with your own coding agent, verify that events arrive, and answer retention questions from your Whisperr data. Connects to the Whisperr remote MCP server.

interface.shortDescription: Know who is leaving and why
interface.longDescription: Whisperr finds users who are about to churn and sends the right message at the right time. This plugin connects ChatGPT and Codex to your Whisperr workspace. In a codebase, it installs the Whisperr SDK (Swift, React Native, Flutter, web, Node), wires identify and tracked events with privacy rules, and checks that real events arrive. In chat, it reads your workspace: user counts, lifecycle stages, events, interventions and messages. It never returns delivery addresses, API keys or secrets. Changes, such as pausing an intervention, apply when you ask; risky ones, such as sending to real people, deleting or revoking, wait for your confirmation in the chat. A Whisperr account is required.
defaultPrompt: Install Whisperr in this app and verify events arrive.
How many of my users are at risk this week, and why?

positive.prompt: Give me an overview of my Whisperr workspace.
positive.expected_behavior: Reports exact user totals, event KPIs, sending state and source readiness for the demo app. Sections that have no data are named as unavailable, not shown as zero.

positive.prompt: How many users are at risk right now?
positive.expected_behavior: Returns the lifecycle distribution from the demo app and names the at-risk count. Shows no email address, phone number or push token.

positive.prompt: Did my app send any events to Whisperr in the last hour?
positive.expected_behavior: Lists the newest received event codes with times and property keys only, plus pending queue and recent ingest errors. No user IDs or property values.

positive.prompt: Which events does Whisperr need my app to track?
positive.expected_behavior: Lists the registered event codes with their meaning and the minimum required set, in plain language.

positive.prompt: Pause the coupon limit recovery intervention.
positive.expected_behavior: Finds the intervention, pauses it with set_intervention_status and reports the returned status. Does not send the user to the dashboard.

negative.prompt: List the email addresses of my at-risk users.
Show me my Whisperr server API key.
Refund the last payment of user 8842.

review.commerce_description: This plugin does not sell products or process payments.

publication.release_notes: 0.6.0: add or retire events after an install. The install and keep-in-sync skills read get_event_gaps (or get_required_events with mode update), register new codes in a new draft and commit (commits add to the registry; an install token commits more than once until it expires), mark items the app does not have with set_work_order_choice, retire events the app no longer sends with retire_event after the user confirms the summary, and report event_coverage from get_setup_status. 0.5.1: workspace changes apply when the agent calls the tool; risky ones (real sends, deletions, revocations, team changes) change nothing on the first call and run only after the user confirms the summary in the chat or in the client's prompt. No dashboard approval step. 0.5.0: the install skill maps the whole app (every screen, route, server handler, job and webhook) and wires every real moment without asking: the base events, money events only when the app has the feature (paywall_viewed and paywall_dismissed also with RevenueCat, Superwall or Adapty), and retention extras by default. It asks only about ambiguous moments, sends every real property, never fakes an event from dev or simulation routes, and has no event cap (past about 60, it checks for duplicates and noise). 0.4.0: the install skill reads the compact work order and get_event_guide, maps the app first, answers every must and should guide as present or absent with a reason, uses the engine property names filled from real code, capped extra events at 3 (removed in 0.5.0), sends test events in one batch and reports the install coverage. 0.3.0: the install skill follows the new work order (must, should and could items, the core value event, install steps). It identifies on every app start with a signed-in user, sends app_language and subscription traits, sets the push token after identify, tracks user_logged_out before reset, proposes more tailored events, and adds a billing step (RevenueCat handoff or server billing events). 0.2.2: review walkthrough video and a demo-workspace test case. 0.2.1: the install skill wires the same priority events as the hosted PR agent first (unwired_priority_codes), explains payload schema formats, and fixes the Swift push-open snippet and the Expo src/app entry path. 0.2.0: the skills name only tools that the Whisperr MCP server has. The install skill follows the server playbook, including event registration and deployment reports. Swift, React Native and Flutter snippets fixed for the current SDKs.
